# Sujātajātaka (Ja 352)

**ID:** Ja 352
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Sujātajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Pious Son Sujāta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the frame story, the Buddha related this discourse while residing at Jetavana to comfort a landowner mourning the death of his father [SuttaCentral]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was reborn as the youth Sujāta [Cunningham 1879]. Seeing his father immobilized by grief, Sujāta began offering grass and water to a dead bovine (described in tradition as a bull or buffalo), pointing out that mourning a departed ancestor whose form is vanished is far more futile than attending to a dead beast whose body is still visible; through this lesson, he successfully extinguished his father's sorrow [Cunningham 1879]. Alexander Cunningham identified a sculpted representation of this Jātaka among the ancient Buddhist coping bas-reliefs at the Bharhut stupa [Cunningham 1879].

SuttaCentral notes several narrative and verse parallels within the Jātaka corpus, specifically the *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449), and *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454), and links the narrative motif to several poems on grief in the *Petavatthu* and *Vimānavatthu* (*Goṇapetavatthu*, Pv 8; *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu*, Pv 17; *Kaṇhapetavatthu*, Pv 18; *Ubbaripetavatthu*, Pv 25; and *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu*, Vv 83) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus matches confirm these relationships, demonstrating extensive Pali-internal text reuse between Ja 352 and Ja 372, Ja 410, Ja 454, Pv 8 (showing extensive verse overlap across §4.1–8.4), Pv 17, Pv 18, Pv 25, and Vv 83, as well as with their corresponding commentaries in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches with score ≥10 [DharmaNexus].
